item: snow_clearing effect_url (Usman, Fu, Miranda-Moreno 2010, TRB paper 10-0774)
note: HTTP 200. The quote is word for word in the abstract. The abstract covers accident frequency during snow-storm events, a road surface condition index (RSI) and a generalized negative binomial (GNB) model. It finds that a 10% better RSI leads to nearly 11% fewer expected accidents. The page shows the TRB 89th Annual Meeting (Jan 10-14, 2010), paper 10-0774, 23 pages and authors that match. The page does not say Ontario or highways; its only highway mention is the keyword 'Highway safety'. That scope is confirmed by Usman's 2011 thesis (checked below: 31 highway routes across Ontario, 2000-2006). Calling it a working paper fits a conference compendium paper.

item: snow_clearing cost_url (SMTC sidewalk snow clearing memo for City of Syracuse)

17-page PDF dated September 18, 2018, from SMTC to Syracuse's Director of Operations. The quote is word for word. It also says the 'University Hill Partnership's sidewalk snow clearing pilot project cost roughly $2,100 per mile during the winter of 2009/2010'. Caveats:
- The $4,000 is a deliberately conservative worst-case planning assumption ('roughly double' University Hill), not an observed cost.
- The memo does not say whether Rochester's $1,400 is per sidewalk mile or per centerline mile. A footnote says mileage means centerline miles unless noted, and the budget math ($25k-$100k gives 6-25 miles) applies $4,000 to centerline miles.
- University Hill was a partnership pilot, not a city program.
The memo also confirms the trigger's ranking by schools and grocery stores.

item: home_repair effect
note: The PMC page served a Google reCAPTCHA page to curl, and WebFetch cannot resolve pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov in this session. I read the full text of the same PMC record (CC-BY) through the NCBI E-utilities efetch API. Confirmed: 13 632 houses on 6732 block faces; 1 Jan 2006 to 30 Apr 2013; total crime -21.9% (IRR 0.78, 0.76-0.80); assault -19.0% (IRR 0.81); robbery -22.6% (IRR 0.77); homicide -21.9% (IRR 0.78); ever-treated blocks -25.4% (IRR 0.75); dose-response (IRR 0.53 for 1 home down to 0.34 for 4 homes); 'grants of up to $20 000'. Also confirmed: JAMA Netw Open 4(7):e2117067. This is a difference-in-differences association, not a randomized trial, and the paper says the violent-subtype effects are driven by the highest-crime areas.

item: home_repair cost
note: PDF read (Divringi, 'Home Repair Costs 2025', December 2025). The table title and the '1939 or Earlier' and '1940-1969' rows match in plain text. The 'All Owner-Occupied Units' row matches in layout-preserving text (plain extraction mixes in the column headers). Appendix Table 2 also has 'Less than 100%' of poverty at an average of $5,886. The table note says medians and averages cover units with repair costs above $0, so 'per home with repair needs' is correct. Data: 2023 AHS PUF plus 2024 RSMeans. The $20,000 BSRP cap is confirmed in the JAMA paper, not in this PDF.

item: code_enforcement effect
note: The PMC page loaded directly. Confirmed: EBL is >= 10 ug/dL; 8.3% (Jul 2004-Jun 2005) fell to 4.4% (Jul 2007-Jun 2008), p = 0.027; 94% passed interior visual inspections in the first 4 years; law adopted 2005, pre-1978 rentals; the housing-market sentence is in the abstract. The authors say a full market analysis was beyond scope, so no price effect was estimated. Caveat: this is a before-after trend with no comparison group, and the decline had already started before the law (Table 4: 8.3%, 6.6%, 5.6%, 4.4%). The authors only say the law 'contributed'. Present it as a trend, not a causal effect. The trigger's rule (block groups holding at least 90% of EBL inspections) is also in the paper.

item: code_enforcement cost
note: Both sentences were found. Context: four new lead inspectors, administration and dust-wipe analysis, about $600,000 a year; city staff estimated about 16,500 units a year; 58,177 interior visual inspections in the first 4 years. $600,000 / 16,500 is about $36, so the arithmetic holds. The $1,726 mean (median $300) is self-reported repair spending from a CGR telephone survey of duplex landlords (183 gave costs). Also confirmed: '$45 million to make > 1,200 units' lead safe, 2003-2009.
